problem.title: Classify installment payment risk tiers
problem.prompt: You are working with a buy-now-pay-later service tracking installment payment compliance, modeled on consumer credit reporting datasets (data.gov). The installment_schedules table has one row per account. Write a query that returns account_id, customer_name, risk_tier, and adjusted_late_fee, ordered by account_id ascending. risk_tier and adjusted_late_fee are computed columns -- build each one exactly as described in Field expectations below.

display.context: You are working with a buy-now-pay-later service tracking installment payment compliance, modeled on consumer credit reporting datasets (data.gov).
display.task: Write a query that returns account_id, customer_name, risk_tier, and adjusted_late_fee from installment_schedules, ordered by account_id ascending; build risk_tier and adjusted_late_fee as described in Field expectations.

table_notes.installment_schedules: one row per customer-plan combination with payment behavior and grace policies

output_field_notes.account_id: the account_id value, copied from installment_schedules
output_field_notes.customer_name: the customer_name value, copied from installment_schedules
output_field_notes.risk_tier: a label of 'low', 'medium', 'high', or 'critical' (see Field expectations for the exact rule)
output_field_notes.adjusted_late_fee: the adjusted late fee rounded to 2 decimals, or NULL when grace_days_allowed is 0 (see Field expectations)

field_logic:
risk_tier: built from days_overdue and grace_days_allowed.
- turn days_overdue into a number: 'never_late' (any case or spaces) becomes 0; NULL or blank becomes 0; otherwise use the number written in days_overdue
- if grace_days_allowed is NULL, use 7
- 'low' when days_overdue = 0
- 'medium' when days_overdue is 1 to 14
- 'high' when days_overdue >= 15 AND days_overdue <= grace_days_allowed
- 'critical' when days_overdue > grace_days_allowed

adjusted_late_fee: built from late_fee and grace_days_allowed.
- if grace_days_allowed = 0, adjusted_late_fee is NULL (avoids divide by zero)
- otherwise adjusted_late_fee = late_fee / (1 + grace_days_allowed), rounded to 2 decimals
edge_cases: If days_overdue is 'never_late' (any case, with or without spaces), treat days_overdue as 0.
If days_overdue is NULL or blank, treat days_overdue as 0.
If grace_days_allowed is 0, adjusted_late_fee is NULL (guards divide by zero).
display.filter_note: All rows from installment_schedules are included.
display.order_by_note: Rows are ordered by account_id ascending.

composite_moves: parse days_overdue text (CASE on 'never_late', NULLIF blank, TO_NUMBER)

hints: You'll need to handle multiple special cases in days_overdue: the text 'never_late' (in any case), NULL values, blank strings, and numeric strings.

Use NULLIF to turn a blank string into NULL, then COALESCE to provide a default. For the 'never_late' text, a CASE expression checking LOWER(TRIM(...)) is helpful. Once you have a numeric overdue value, build a CASE ladder with multiple WHEN branches for the tier bands.

Convert days_overdue with: CASE WHEN LOWER(TRIM(COALESCE(days_overdue, ''))) = 'never_late' THEN 0 ELSE COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(days_overdue), '')::INT, 0) END. Fill grace with COALESCE(grace_days_allowed, 7). For adjusted_late_fee, compute late_fee / NULLIF(1 + COALESCE(grace_days_allowed, 7), 1) and ROUND to 2 decimals. The tier logic compares effective_overdue against 0, 14, and effective_grace.
problem.answer_key:
WITH parsed AS (
  SELECT
    account_id,
    customer_name,
    late_fee,
    COALESCE(grace_days_allowed, 7) AS effective_grace,
    CASE
      WHEN LOWER(TRIM(COALESCE(days_overdue, ''))) = 'never_late' THEN 0
      ELSE COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(days_overdue), '')::INT, 0)
    END AS effective_overdue
  FROM installment_schedules
)
SELECT
  account_id,
  customer_name,
  CASE
    WHEN effective_overdue = 0 THEN 'low'
    WHEN effective_overdue BETWEEN 1 AND 14 THEN 'medium'
    WHEN effective_overdue > effective_grace THEN 'critical'
    ELSE 'high'
  END AS risk_tier,
  ROUND(late_fee / NULLIF(1 + effective_grace, 1), 2) AS adjusted_late_fee
FROM parsed
ORDER BY account_id;

_meta.scenario: a buy-now-pay-later service tracking installment payment compliance
_meta.instructions_rewritten: 2026-06-29: rewrote field_logic/prompt/edge_cases to use exact column names only, no invented aliases, one rule per bullet

user_solution:
/* notes */
WITH base AS (
    SELECT
        account_id,
        customer_name,
        (CASE WHEN (LOWER(TRIM(days_overdue)) = 'never_late' OR LOWER(TRIM(days_overdue)) IS NULL OR LOWER(TRIM(days_overdue)) = '') THEN 0 ELSE days_overdue::int END)::INT AS days_overdue,
        CASE WHEN grace_days_allowed IS NULL THEN 7 ELSE grace_days_allowed::int END AS grace_days_allowed,
        late_fee
    FROM installment_schedules
)
SELECT
    account_id,
    customer_name,
    CASE WHEN days_overdue = 0 THEN 'low'
        WHEN days_overdue >= 1 AND days_overdue <= 14 THEN 'medium'
        WHEN days_overdue >= 15 AND days_overdue <= grace_days_allowed THEN 'high'
        WHEN days_overdue > grace_days_allowed THEN 'critical'
    END AS risk_tier,
    ROUND(CASE 
        WHEN grace_days_allowed = 0 THEN NULL 
        ELSE late_fee / NULLIF(1 + grace_days_allowed, 0) 
    END, 2) AS adjusted_late_fee
FROM base
ORDER BY 1;
